page: Microsoft Azure D8s_v6 is a general purpose virtual machine instance running on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz with 4 physical cores and 8 dedicated vCPUs via simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is balanced at 32.0 GB of RAM, offering exactly 4.0 GB per vCPU. The processor architecture includes 260 MB of L3 cache alongside specialized instruction extensions, such as AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and VAES cryptography acceleration. The instance does not include local ephemeral storage or integrated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached Premium Storage.

Performance benchmarks place the D8s_v6 squarely within the middle 50th percentile across most compute, memory, and application-level workloads. It achieves a Geekbench multi-core score of 6709.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 14296.51. In memory-intensive testing, it produces uncached read bandwidth of 67.85 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 46.43 GB/sec. Application testing shows solid general utility, delivering 11.42 million Redis SET operations per second and 15.06 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. CPU-bound machine learning inference runs acceptably on small 135M parameter models, but larger models highlight compute bottlenecks, such as a weak text generation rate of 7.94 tokens per second on a 7B model.

From an infrastructure perspective, the D8s_v6 provides predictable performance for workloads that benefit from a standard 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio without paying for unused GPU silicon or dedicated local NVMe drives. Its balanced profile makes it suitable for application backends, mid-tier relational databases using remote storage, software compilation pipelines, and containerized enterprise services.
description: Microsoft Azure D8s_v6 is a general purpose virtual machine instance driven by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz. The hardware layout features 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores, 32.0 GB of system memory, and a 260 MB L3 cache. It incorporates vector and matrix acceleration instructions, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX, while omitting bundled local storage and discrete GPUs. Across synthetic and real-world benchmarks, the instance consistently exhibits average tier throughput, achieving 11.42 million Redis operations per second, a PassMark score of 14296.51, and 15.06 GB/sec in static web serving. Lacking local storage, it relies on network storage solutions. The D8s_v6 serves as a balanced compute platform well aligned with enterprise web serving, microservice hosting, CI/CD compilation, and medium-scale database workloads requiring stable dedicated CPU capacity.
